correctness.rationale: After any prefix the undominated cells are the intersection of the row-column crosses of chosen vertices. The three exhaustive cases for the first two cells give the exact number of terminal third moves and nonterminal third plus forced fourth moves. A bipartite edge-cover reduction classifies minimal four-sets and gives exactly 24 permutations per minimal set. Algebraic subtraction yields the redundant-history count; conditional uniform-next-choice counting yields the online law. Every boundary m,n>=2 and distinctness is handled. Separately implemented original-adjacency full history checker passed 15 dimension pairs (2<=m<=n<=6), 1,469,556 ordered terminal histories, minimality comparisons and exact rational online laws; experiments are corroboration, not universal proof.

value.rationale: Exact legal-history multiplicities matter in sequential open-neighborhood coverage where different sequences can end on the same dominating set. The formula quantifies nontrivial redundancy of length-four completions exactly and establishes the sharp m,n>=3 threshold; it also proves an opposite q->infinity limit for sampling uniformly over finished histories versus uniformly at each legal step. These are behaviorally distinct natural sampling methods whose disagreement is not encoded in known scalar Grundy values or final-set enumerators.
